label: text
text: At the first call-over for the St. Leger at the Victoria Club to-day, Manna was installed as favourite. The price was 4/1 against (taken and offered).

label: text
text: [Note]: The St. Leger is the last of the season's classic races on the Home turf. It will be over 1¼ miles and 132 yards and will be run at Doncaster on September 9. Mr. Henry Morrisz of Shanghai is the owner of Manna which won the Derby in rather sensational fashion but has since been defeated when conceding weight to improved rivals.]

label: text
text: In the final of the Newport Invitation (lawn tennis) Singles Bowl, W. M. Johnston (U.S.A.) beat B. I. C. Norton (South Africa) 6-3, 6-3, 6-3, winning the trophy outright.

label: text
text: In the doubles W. M. Johnston and C. J. Griffin (U.S.A.) beat B. I. C. Norton (South Africa) and Ray Casey (U.S.A.) 6-2, 6-1, 5-7, 2-6, 6-1.

label: text
text: [Note: Johnston is one of America's Davis Cup team and ranks second or third in the world's list. Norton plays at Wimbledon a few years ago and nearly beat W. T. Tilden, the world champion. Since then he has been resident in America where he has been in the front rank. Griffin excelled a few years ago and his name also appears in the national championship records. Casey is one of America's juniors; he was at Wimbledon this year where he played with credit.]

Miss Helen Wills (U.S.A.) retained the Women's National Lawn Tennis championship by defending Miss K. McKane (Britain), in the final, 8-6, 6-0, 6-2.
[Note: A British lady has yet to win the American singles title in recent years although Miss McKane and Mrs. B. C. Covell won the doubles in 1923. In 1924 Miss McKane beat Miss Wills in the Wimbledon final, but subsequently lost to the American girl on several occasions. Miss Wills was champion in 1923 and 1924.]

label: text
text: The following letter has been addressed to Mr. P. H. Holyoak by Mr. Chang Tui-piu, representing the Trade Maintenance Committee of Kwangtung Province:

label: text
text: Dear Sir,—As temporary residents in Hongkong, we wish to assure, through you, our friends outside Canton that the people of Kwangtung have not been unaware of the approaching dangers of Bolshevism and have in the last two years repeatedly, unceasingly fought them by voicing protests against all harmful acts, refusing to pay all unjust and unreasonable taxes whenever possible and, at least once, met the Bolsheviks arms to arms. In our earlier struggles we had not received any moral or material encouragement from outside.

label: text
text: Our people of Kwangtung real, be the close relationship, and mutual interest in inter-dependence on each other between Canton and Hongkong; are fully congizant of the fact that further delay in the return to normal trade will result in economic ruin in all parts of South China, are not blind to the treachery of Bolsheviks taking shelter behind the patriotism of the students and dissatisfaction within the workers, and clearly understand that the Bolsheviks intend to cover their violation of treaty spirit with the announcement that strikers have the privilege of refusing service to persons or parties they have reasons to oppose or disagree with.

label: text
text: We are afraid that Bolshevism will respect no diplomatic settlements and that the authorities at Peking and those in other capitals have not been thoroughly acquainted with the local situation in South China.

label: text
text: It may be of interest to you for us to point out again that the people of Kwangtung are not at all inactive in their desire to oust the evils and dangers of Bolshevism from their territory, that their seeming inertia has been forced by circumstances which they are still unable to overcome, and that, as soon as necessary and proper arrangements are perfected, necessary steps will be taken to recover the power and the government now usurped by a party- of Holshevists whom no responsible persons inside or outside

label: text
text:
Your indignation over the acts of Bolsheviks in places where foreign interests as well as Chinese are affected and your desire to see an early restoration of peace and trade have our sympathy; appreciation, and gratitude and we shall not hesitate to assure you that we are not by any means slow in our plan and effort to get rid of a curse and danger now cursing not only China but all other parts of the world wherever Bolsheviks may be found.
Since Bolsheviks has become a world curse and is bringing suffering to all mankind, it should be destroyed as a common enemy to mankind wherever it may be found, and the question of removing a common enemy should not touch that of national, political, or territorial issues or jurisdictions.

label: text
text: Being likewise cursed by Bolshevism, the people of Kwangthong are watching with deep interest the manner the people of Hongkong will adopt to lessen evils now being spread by Bolsheviats in this part of the world.

label: text
text: As will be seen from the announcement by Hongkong Amusements, Ltd., the Colony is to have the pleasure of welcoming back old favourites to the Star Theatre next Thursday, Friday and Saturday when Mr. Wallingford Tate and Mr. Jack Crichton will present the Broadcasters Co. in miniature revue.

label: text
text: Three members of this Company last visited Hongkong with that successful combination known as the Globe Trotters, and patrons of the Theatre are assured a bright performance.

label: text
text: Mr. Crichton will also be remembered as the principal comedian of the last Bandman Opera Co. that visited Hongkong where he made a big hit in Afgar, Irene, Bran Pie, etc. Mr. Tate's pianistic skill and character sketches are well known throughout the East.

label: text
text: This present Company has now toured the East for over eighteen months and is now passing through to play return dates at Rangoon, Calcutta and Bombay, so the Star audiences are assured of a really first-class entertainment.

label: text
text: Of the ladies, Miss Bobby Broadhurst, the well-known Australian Contralto, will again charm us as she did with the Globe Trotters, while Miss Lucina, who has recently been playing with the Dolly Sisters in Paris comes to Hongkong with all the latest American songs and dancers.
